label: RoPA · Record of Processing Activities
refTag: DATA FOUNDATION · FEEDS s.5 NOTICES, s.11 ACCESS, DPIA
description: Jethur discovers your processing activities and builds the RoPA for you — evidence-backed drafts, human-approved, continuously monitored. Related purposes are grouped into meaningful activities; you validate, owners sign off.
emptyTitle: Your RoPA is empty — let Jethur AI build it with you
emptyDescriptionWithEvidence: I've read your Data Map ({datasets} dataset{datasetsPlural} across {sources} source{sourcesPlural}), so I know what you hold and where. The 2-minute interview collects what scanners can't see — who the data belongs to, why you process it, who you share it with — and I draft every activity for owner sign-off.
emptyDescriptionNoEvidence: Nothing is scanned yet, so I have no evidence to start from. The 2-minute interview still works: I'll ask who the data belongs to, why you process it and who you share it with, and draft every activity for owner sign-off.
emptyOrLabel: or draft one activity at a time
secondaryCta: Draft one activity at a time
quickDraftHint: Jethur fills the purpose, data types, lawful basis, retention and owner — you review and save.
emptyHintLine: DRAFTS ONLY — NOTHING COUNTS AS EVIDENCE UNTIL A HUMAN OWNER CONFIRMS
toastExport: Audit-ready RoPA report (PDF/XLSX) generated — includes change history
toastGenerate: Jethur AI is reading your Data Map and will draft activities for your review.
kpiUnlinkedDatasets: Data Map datasets without an activity

infoModalDescription: Jethur reads your Data Map, asks only what scans can't answer, and keeps approved activities under watch.
infoModalPanelSub: Draft-only — a human owner always confirms before an activity counts as evidence.
infoModalStep1Body: Data categories, sources and volumes come from your Data Map findings — never from guesswork.
infoModalStep2Body: Jethur asks only what evidence can't establish — and "Unknown" is always an acceptable answer. Inferred vs confirmed is always labelled.
infoModalStep3Body: Related purposes are clustered into meaningful processing activities — each with evidence, confidence, a suggested basis (s.6/s.7) and a sourced retention rule, or an honest "Unknown".
infoModalMonitorSub: Approved activities are watched — changes reopen review, nothing drifts silently.
wizardDescription: Describe the activity in plain language — Jethur turns it into a RoPA record, then the owner you name confirms it.
step1Sub: Describe this activity the way you'd explain it to a customer — no legal language needed.
wizardNameHint: The name your team already uses for this work.
wizardPurposeHint: One plain sentence — this exact line appears in your privacy notice.
wizardPurposePlaceholder: e.g. Deliver products ordered by customers
wizardPurposeError: Describe the purpose in one line
wizardPrincipalsHint: The people this activity is about.
wizardMinorsWarning: Under-18 data: the law is strict here — you need a parent's verifiable consent, and tracking or targeted ads are banned (s.9, penalties up to ₹200 crore). I've pre-selected the right settings.
wizardIdentifiersHint: Tap all that apply — red ones are sensitive and get extra protection.
wizardIdentifiersError: Pick at least one data type
wizardCollectionPartner: From a partner or third party
wizardStorageHint: The apps and databases that store it — pick from your connected sources.
wizardLawfulBasisLabel: Why are you allowed to use this data?
wizardLawfulBasisHint: Pick the one that matches — this is your "lawful basis" under the DPDP Act.
wizardBasisError: Choose why you're allowed to process this
wizardBasisConsentDesc: You asked clearly and they agreed — e.g. a signup tick-box.
wizardBasisVoluntaryDesc: They handed it over for this exact purpose — e.g. address for delivery.
wizardBasisEmploymentDesc: Payroll, HR records, protecting the company.
wizardProcessorsHint: Companies that handle it for you — couriers, payment gateways, tools.
wizardRetentionLabel: How long do you keep it?
wizardAdvancedToggle: Advanced — already filled with sensible defaults
wizardOperationsHint: What you actually do with the data (s.2).

toastValidationFinal: Pick a lawful basis and an owner to finish

detailEvidenceSub: The sources behind this draft — never invented.

generateTitle: Generate your RoPA with Jethur AI
generateIntro: Four steps, about two minutes. I start from the evidence in your Data Map and ask only what scans can't answer — "Unknown" is always a valid answer, and nothing counts as evidence until an owner confirms.
generateStepperLabel: Generate your RoPA with Jethur AI
generateAiIntroWithEvidence: I've read your Data Map — {datasets} datasets across {sources} sources. Below is what the evidence suggests — each card shows its evidence and my confidence. Confirm what actually applies; nothing here is invented.
generateAiIntroNoEvidence: Nothing has been scanned yet, so I have no evidence to lean on — these are the usual starting points for an Indian SME. Confirm what actually applies; nothing here is invented.
generatePrincipalsTitle: Whose personal data do you process?
generatePrincipalsSub: Data Principal categories — suggested from evidence.
generatePurposesTitle: What do you use personal data for?
generatePurposesSub: Jethur found these potential purposes from your data and systems. Confirm what actually applies.
generateSourcesTitle: Where does personal data come from?
generateSourcesSub: Sources of personal data — pick all that apply.
generateIdentifiedBannerWithEvidence: Jethur identified {count} potential processing activities from {datasets} datasets across {sources} sources. Related purposes are grouped into meaningful activities — you review the grouping before anything is generated.
generateIdentifiedBannerNoEvidence: Jethur identified {count} potential processing activities from your answers — no scan evidence yet. Related purposes are grouped into meaningful activities — you review the grouping before anything is generated.
generateStep2AiIntro: s.11 gives every person the right to know who their data was shared with. I separate processors (work on your behalf, s.8(2) contract needed) from other recipients (receive data in their own right).
generateProcessorsSub: Organisations processing personal data on your behalf.
generateRecipientsSub: Receive data for their own purpose — not processors.
generateLocationTitle: Where is personal data processed or stored?
generateLocationSub: I won't conclude "India only" from one hosting region — other processing locations need your confirmation.
generateRetentionSub: I never invent retention periods — rules I've found are shown with their source.
generateRetentionLawCaption: e.g. GST · 8 yrs, KYC/PMLA — from configured rules
generateRetentionUnknownCaption: No policy exists yet — honest answer
generateRetentionLawHint: Suggested: 8 years for billing · Source: Configured GST/accounting retention rule (HIGH) · KYC/PMLA & log rules also found.
generateRetentionUnknownHint: Activities without a legal rule will be drafted with Retention: Unknown and flagged to resolve — never guessed.
generateStep3AiIntro: Each processing activity gets its own owner — their sign-off becomes your evidence. I've suggested owners from your Employee register with my reasoning; change any of them.
generateQualitySub: I flag my own weak spots before you generate.
generateQualityNeedsReview: {count} activities — confirm details during owner sign-off
generateValidationSelectOne: Select at least one principal and one purpose to continue
generateValidationConfirmLocation: Confirm where personal data is processed — "Unknown" is a valid answer
generateToastGenerated: Drafted {count} activities — sent to owners for review
generateToastReviewIssues: Fix retention or location here — or resolve per-activity after generation
